---
title: "R Markdown basics"
output: html_document
---

R Markdown mixes writing and R. The writing is plain text, with a few
marks for style: **bold**, *italic*, and `code`. Each grey block below is
a chunk. Press Run chunk on its header to run it, or Render above the
script to make the finished page.

```{r}
planets <- read.csv("data/exoplanets.csv")
```

## A number in a sentence

The Open Exoplanet Catalogue lists `r nrow(planets)` confirmed planets
around other stars. `r sum(planets$year >= 2014, na.rm = TRUE)` of them were
found from 2014 on, most by the Kepler space telescope watching stars dim
as a planet passed in front. Those numbers come from R when the page is
rendered, so they are never out of date.

## A table

```{r}
head(planets[, c("name", "method", "year", "mass_jupiter")])
```

## A plot

```{r, fig.height = 4}
barplot(table(planets$year), las = 2, col = "#1F5F8B", border = NA,
        cex.names = 0.7, ylab = "Planets found")
```

## Hiding the code

Add `echo = FALSE` to a chunk and only its result shows on the page.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
sort(table(planets$method), decreasing = TRUE)
```
